slides.title: Sorting & Partitioning
slides.prompt: Sorting algorithms reorder elements according to a comparator. Partitioning reorganizes elements so that those satisfying a predicate precede those that do not.

slides.title: Basic Sorting
slides.prompt: Fill in the function used to sort a range into ascending order.

slides.title: Stable Sort Guarantee
slides.prompt: What operational guarantee does std::stable_sort provide over std::sort?
options: Preserves the relative order of equivalent elements
Runs faster on completely unsorted ranges
slides.correctAnswer: Preserves the relative order of equivalent elements

slides.title: Partitioning Range
slides.prompt: Fill in the algorithm that reorders elements such that elements matching the predicate come first.
slides.codeSnippet: auto bound = std::___(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x){ return x % 2 == 0; });

slides.title: std::partial_sort Purpose
slides.prompt: When would you choose std::partial_sort over std::sort?
options: When you only need the smallest N elements sorted at the beginning of a container
When sorting strings instead of numbers
When memory usage must be zero
slides.correctAnswer: When you only need the smallest N elements sorted at the beginning of a container

slides.title: Nth Element Algorithm
slides.prompt: Fill in the algorithm that places the element that would be at position N in a fully sorted range, rearranging other elements around it.

slides.title: std::is_partitioned Function
slides.prompt: What does std::is_partitioned(begin, end, pred) check?
options: Whether all elements satisfying the predicate precede all elements that do not
Whether the container is divided into two equal length halves
Whether elements are sorted in ascending order
Whether duplicate elements are grouped together
slides.correctAnswer: Whether all elements satisfying the predicate precede all elements that do not
